newsitem.title: CHINA: China to remove import curbs after WTO entry.
newsitem.headline: China to remove import curbs after WTO entry.

text.p: China plans to gradually remove restrictions on 385 categories of imports after gaining entry into the World Trade Organisation (WTO), the China Chemical Industry News said on Wednesday.
Import restrictions on nautical diesel engines would be removed by the end of 1997, the newspaper said, quoting unidentified sources.
On entry to the WTO, China plans to cut restrictions on the import of 66 categories of goods, including sheep's wool, tobacco-related products and film, the newspaper said.
In the first three years after entry, 69 categories of goods would have their import restrictions lifted, including chemical fibre, tape recorders and medical equipment, it said.
In the fourth and fifth years after entry, China plans to lift import curbs on 38 categories, including televisions, refrigerators and printers, the newspaper said.
In the sixth to eighth years after entry, import restrictions on 113 categories would be lifted, including motorbikes, air-conditioners and watches, it said.
From the eighth to twelfth years after entry, import curbs on 86 categories would be removed, including machine tools and construction equipment and 50 kinds of car components, it said.
Existing members of the WTO have called on China to make new offers on the terms of its long-delayed entry to the global trade club.
